newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA STUMBLE IN MASSIVE RUN CHASE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA STUMBLE IN MASSIVE RUN CHASE.

text.p: South Africa, set a victory target of 461 by Indian skipper Sachin Tendulkar, were precariously placed on 58 for three at tea on the fourth day of the third and final test on Wednesday.

South Africa suffered an early blow when left-hander Gary Kirsten, who scored centuries in both innings of the second test at Calcutta, was trapped leg before for seven by Javagal Srinath with a delivery which cut in and kept low.

Herschelle Gibbs was bowled by Venkatesh Prasad for five through a bat-pad gap and Darryl Cullinan, at the non-striker's end, was run out for two by a direct hit from Tendulkar at mid-off. Andrew Hudson (19) and skipper Hansie Cronje (17) were the unbeaten batsmen at the interval.
India, 270 for five overnight, declared their second innings at their lunch score of 400-7 and set the South Africans a target never achieved by a side batting last in 120 years of test cricket.
Mohammed Azharuddin's finished on 163 not out, his sixth-wicket stand of 165 with Rahul Dravid setting an Indian record for any wicket against South Africa.
